The '''Players Committee advocates''' are the volunteer leaders of the [[Players Committee]], each responsible for an area such as rules, design, tournaments or marketing. Early sources call them Player Advocates or the Advocate Council.

The Players Committee was set up by Decipher itself. After Decipher lost the rights to make the card game and stopped printing it, the company worked with Lucasfilm to give stewardship of the game to members of the playing community.<ref name="about2008">[https://web.archive.org/web/20080925005351/http://www.swccgpc.com/about/ Who We Are], swccgpc.com (Wayback, 25 September 2008)</ref> In a letter dated 25 January 2002, Decipher's chairman and chief executive Warren Holland wrote that, after the licence announcement, the company had received an overwhelming number of emails from players who wanted to be involved; from those requests Decipher selected a core team of representatives to work on behalf of the community, with the aim of turning the game over to the players.<ref name="pc1" /> The letter named the first six Player Advocates.

Each row below lists the full roster from the month it was first documented until the next row. The current roster is on [[Players Committee#Current advocates|the main article]].
